entry.title: What Should I do If my T2353/Omni E25/T2352/Omni E28 shows clean water insufficient and downgrade to vacuum-only mode, or displays the error messages code-6536 Insufficient clean water, switched to Vacuum-Only mode, code-6537, the task was automatically downgraded to Vacuum-Only mode?
entry.content:
To resolve the issue you're experiencing, please follow the steps below:



Check the clean water tank in the base station. If it's empty, fill it with water and then restart the cleaning task. In most cases, this simple step will resolve the problem.

If your robot vacuum starts a task on the same floor where the base station is located, and the issue persists after refilling the water tank and starting a new mopping task, please feel free to contact us for further assistance.



Please note: The alert you see is just a reminder from the device. When the robot is operating on a floor without a base station, and the clean water runs low, it will automatically switch to pure vacuum mode to continue the cleaning task. This is a normal protective mechanism designed to ensure the task can still run smoothly even when you're not at home.



If the problem continues after refilling the water and starting a new mopping task, don't hesitate to reach out to us again. We're here to help.

entry.title: what should I do when T2080 S1 Pro has EB1L: The robot encountered an error while adding clean water. Task ended/Robot injecting clean water abnormally?
entry.content:
1. Remove the clean water tank from the base station and check the seal ring of the outlet hole to ensure that it is installed correctly. Have the user shine a flashlight on the clean water tank pipe to check whether the pipe inside the clean water tank is damaged.

https://d3pkbgk01oouhl.cloudfront.net/upload_file/prod/the-silicone-rubber-sealing-ring-for-clean-water-outlet.png

https://d3pkbgk01oouhl.cloudfront.net/upload_file/prod/check-the-pipe-of-clean-water-tank.png

2. Fill the water tank with clean water to the maximum water level, then ensure the water tank is securely placed in the base station.

3. Check the robot's water inlet for debris or blockages, then clean with a paper towel or cotton swab.

https://d3pkbgk01oouhl.cloudfront.net/upload_file/prod/water-filling-interface.png

4. After the error occurs, remove the robot from the base station and check the rubber plug at the base station's water inlet to see if there is any water. Additionally, check if the rubber plug is damaged or missing.

https://d3pkbgk01oouhl.cloudfront.net/upload_file/prod/Silicone-for-base-station-water-injection2.png

5. Update the firmware to version 7.0.143 or higher.

entry.title: What should I do if my Breast Pump S1 Pro (T8D04) has no suction at all?
entry.content:
For the S1 Pro breast pump with no suction issue, follow these troubleshooting steps: 
1. Factory Reset: Press and hold the Power button and + button simultaneously for about 5 seconds to restore factory settings, then try again. 
2. Test Main Unit: Remove the pump hub, place the suction port against your palm, and start the device to test suction. If you feel suction, the main unit works fine and the issue may be with tubes, breast shield, or other accessories. If no suction, the unit needs repair. 
3. Check Assembly and Sealing: Verify the breast shield, silicone pad, and valve are correctly installed. Check if the sealing ring is damaged, aged, or blocked. 
4. Check Valve Condition: Remove the one-way valve or duckbill valve, inspect for deformation, and ensure it opens and closes freely without milk residue blockage. 
5. Check Tubing and Connections: Confirm both ends of the tube are firmly connected. Check for cracks or hardening. 
6. Confirm Mode and Level: Check if the device is in Letdown Mode (lighter suction). Switch to Expression Mode and adjust to an appropriate level. 
7. Check Battery Level: Low battery may cause reduced suction. Fully charge before retrying. 
8. Reset Device: Press and hold the power button for 12 seconds to reset, then try again. 
9. If there is still no suction after all steps, please upload device logs for further assistance.

entry.title: What should I do if eufy Wearable Breast Pump S1 Pro(T8D04) has weak or no suction?
entry.content:
1. Inspect the duckbill valve and diaphragm for damage (cracks, chips, holes, or tears). If damaged, discontinue use and replace. 
2. Check that the assembly is correct --- ensure the four components (duckbill valve, flange tunnel, diaphragm, pump hub) are perfectly sealed. 
3. Ensure the flange is properly sealed against your breast with no air gaps. 
4. Check the battery level --- low battery may reduce suction performance.

entry.title: Why does my Breast Pump S1 Pro (T8D04) motor make a clicking sound but no suction?
entry.content:
If the motor of your Breast Pump S1 Pro (T8D04) makes a clicking sound but there is no suction, you can try the following steps to troubleshoot: 

1. Restore factory settings: 
Press and hold the "power button" and the "+" button simultaneously for about 5 seconds. The device will restore to factory settings. After restoring factory settings, try using the breast pump again. If the problem persists, proceed to the next step. 

2. Check if the main unit is working properly: 
Remove the main head, align the suction port with your palm, and test if there is suction after the device starts. 
If you feel a significant suction on your palm, it indicates that the main unit is working properly, and the problem may be with other components (such as the hose or the breast pump cover). 
If there is no suction, further troubleshooting may be needed. 

3. Inspect the key components: 
Inspect the duckbill valve and diaphragm for damage, including cracks, chips, holes, or tears. If a part is damaged, discontinue use and purchase a replacement. 
Check that the assembly is correct and that the four pieces (duckbill valve, flange tunnel, diaphragm, and pump hub) are perfectly sealed.
